name: Sölden
kurzbeschreibung: Sölden is the heart of the Ötztal – glacier skiing, 007-Elements, and a buzzing Après-Ski scene.
beschreibung:
Overview

Sölden is located at an altitude of 1,368 meters in the upper Ötztal valley in the Imst district, surrounded by the soaring glaciated peaks of the Ötztal and Stubai Alps. Covering more than 467 square kilometers, Sölden is Austria's second-largest municipality by land area after Vienna, stretching all the way to Mount Wildspitze (3,768 m), North Tyrol’s highest peak. Home to roughly 3,200 residents, the community comprises the vibrant valley hub, the ski-in/ski-out resort of Hochsölden (2,090 m), twin glacier ski arenas, and the peaceful mountaineering village of Vent (1,895 m). As a world-class alpine sports destination, Sölden offers two glacier ski areas, three lift-accessible peaks over 3,000 meters (the famous BIG 3), and cutting-edge cable cars. In summer, the town transforms into a premier mountain biking Mecca with the Bike Republic Sölden.

History

The settlement was first documented around 1150 as seldon, deriving from a Middle High German term denoting a modest peasant holding. For centuries, high-alpine subsistence farming and transhumance cattle drives over glaciated passes into South Tyrol defined daily life. The modern tourism revolution began with glacier development: the Rettenbachferner ski area and glacier road opened in 1975, followed in 1982 by the construction of the Rosi Mittermaier Tunnel at 2,829 meters to connect the Tiefenbachferner glacier. Since the late 1990s, Sölden has hosted the traditional late-October FIS Alpine Ski World Cup season opener. International cinematic fame arrived in 2014/2015 when director Sam Mendes chose Sölden and the ice Q summit restaurant on Gaislachkogl as a key shooting location for the James Bond film SPECTRE. The late Gothic parish church in Rettenbach dates back to 1288.

Getting there

Sölden is safely accessible year-round from the Inn Valley. By car, leave the A12 Inntal motorway at the Ötztal exit and follow federal highway B186 (Ötztalstraße) for approximately 35 kilometers south through Längenfeld into Sölden. In summer (June to October), the toll Timmelsjoch High Alpine Road (2,509 m) provides a dramatic scenic link to South Tyrol and Merano. Train travelers alight at Ötztal-Bahnhof on the Arlberg mainline, served by ÖBB Railjet and Eurocity trains. VVT regional bus line 320 runs every 15 to 30 minutes from the station straight to Sölden and Obergurgl. Ski shuttle buses throughout the valley floor are free for lift pass holders.

Tips

Experience the BIG 3, the trio of 3,000-meter peaks accessible by cable car: Gaislachkogl (3,056 m) with the futuristic ice Q restaurant, Tiefenbachkogl (3,250 m) with its hanging glass Skywalk bridge, and Schwarze Schneid (3,340 m) offering 360-degree views to the Dolomites. Film enthusiasts must tour 007 ELEMENTS, an underground James Bond cinematic installation built inside the summit of Gaislachkogl. Mountain bikers can ride the purpose-built flow trails of Bike Republic Sölden. For authentic mountain solitude, visit the historic mountaineering village of Vent, the birthplace of the German-Austrian Alpine Club at the foot of the Wildspitze.
